function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and can include optional query parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

search.description: Query parameter to search for a specific term.

limit.description: Query parameter to limit the number of results.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to include in the request as key-value pairs.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Authorization.description: Authorization credentials for connecting to the resource.

timeout.description: The amount of time to wait for a server response, in seconds. This is a float type value.

If your “$21 bn” refers to a different metric—such as revenue from a single product line, a regional market, or a shorter reporting period—I’d love to help clarify. Which timeframe or segment were you thinking of?
